name: 11-dim-lightson-20260816
incident: kinder-links 2026-08-16, run 2 (the magnitude the fast path cannot have)
description:
The backstop half of scenario 10, and the honest statement of what the sustained-brightening hold can and cannot do. The hold's bar is (100+day_gain_pct)/200 of the resting level, times the 0.97 arming margin - so it needs a 22.4% brightening before it will even start counting. That number is a design choice, not an accident: below it the machine would be spending audible IR-cut clicks on light changes it cannot distinguish from AGC drift. But it means there is a real, sustained, permanent class of light-on event that is simply too small for the fast path, and the machine must still recover from it - just not in 30s.

This is that event, at the incident's own magnitude. kinder-links' run 2 moved the night pipeline 2233 -> 1649, but the baseline it was measured against was NOT 2233: the light had been on before run 1, dragging the baseline down, and 75s of darkness recovers almost nothing of a 250s-tau EMA. So the effective brightening against the reference was around 12%, half of what the hold requires. Here that is replayed directly: a settled night at 2000, then a permanent step to 1750 (12.5%) while the day pipeline drops to 250 - i.e. the mode is genuinely, visibly wrong, and the fast path genuinely cannot see it.

WHAT IT ASSERTS. The forbid_log is the point: `sustained brightening` must NOT appear. If a future change to the hold's bar, its arming margin or its frozen reference makes this fire, that is a sensitivity regression and it will show up here as a failure rather than as a fleet-wide increase in IR-cut clicking six weeks later. What must happen instead is the slow path: the step is measurably brighter than the frozen probe anchor, min_smooth_since_probe latches it, the x2 backoff is suspended, and the periodic reconfirm lands one un-backed-off night_reconfirm_s after arming - t=1212 against a light that came on at t=1000, i.e. 202s, comfortably inside the 900s the design-notes invariant promises. The day pipeline confirms day and it sticks.

So the two scenarios together pin the whole ladder: 10 says a 27% light-on is caught in ~34s by the hold, 11 says a 12.5% one is caught in ~200s by the reconfirm, and neither is allowed to drift into the other's job.

expect_log: lowest since the last probe.*suspending it
